threads.body: perhaps it would be safer to check that the expected method `newInterceptor` is called

perhaps it would be better to just invoke other methods on the original instance
```suggestion
                  return method.invoke(builder, args);
```

In the proxy invocation handler, non-"newInterceptor" calls are forwarded to the ManagedChannelBuilder instance (method.invoke(builder, ...)). For Object methods this changes proxy semantics (e.g., proxy.equals(builder) can become true via builder.equals(builder)) and can cause surprising behavior if gRPC ever calls equals/hashCode on the factory. Handle Object methods explicitly (identity-based equals/hashCode/toString), and avoid invoking factory-interface methods on the builder instance.

replies.body: Fixed in 3c7ab54fc0157a127cbf1bc886ca2dfb9820ceda — `Object` methods (`equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`) now use identity semantics rather than being forwarded to the `ManagedChannelBuilder` instance.

threads.body: The authority parsing helpers split on the first ':' which breaks IPv6 authorities like "[::1]:8080" (host becomes "[" and port parse fails). Since this code is now the fallback path when a target isn't available, it will produce incorrect server.address/server.port for IPv6 endpoints. Consider reusing the bracket-aware parsing logic from GrpcTargetParser (or implement equivalent handling here).

replies.body: Fixed in 96342415fe235fc6f9ef33c220d184cf704afff5 — promoted the bracket-aware parser in `GrpcTargetParser` to a `parseAuthority(...)` helper and routed both the client fallback and `createServerRequest` through it, so authority and target parsing share a single source of truth.

threads.body: `parseHostPort("")` currently returns a `ParsedTarget` with an empty-string address. That can lead to emitting `server.address=""` (empty) on spans when the target/authority endpoint is empty (e.g., `dns:///`). Consider returning `null` for empty input (and letting callers treat it as unavailable) to avoid setting invalid semconv attributes.

When the input is `host:port` but the port is missing/invalid (e.g., `"myhost:"` or `"myhost:abc"`), `parseHostPort` returns the full original string as the address. This regresses the previous behavior (host extracted, port omitted) and can result in `server.address` incorrectly containing a colon/port fragment. Consider returning `host` with a null port when `parsePort(...)` fails (and add a unit test for this case).

`GrpcRequest.createClientRequest(...)` / `createServerRequest(...)` are `public` but appear to be used only internally by this instrumentation. Exposing them expands the public API surface of `GrpcRequest` and makes future refactors harder; consider making these factories package-private unless there is an explicit external use case.

`parseHostPort` can return a `ParsedTarget` with an empty `address` for inputs like ":8080" or ":" (host part empty). That would result in emitting `server.address=""`, which is not a valid value for semconv. Consider treating an empty host as unavailable (return `null`) and add a unit test covering this case.

replies.body: Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/16161/commits/1be97271398 — `parseHostPort` now returns `null` when the host is empty (including `[]:port`), and `parse()` routes bracketed inputs through it. Added tests for `:8080`, `:`, `[]:8080`, and `[]`.

threads.body: In the unix/unix-abstract `://` parsing branch, `rest` can be empty (e.g., `unix://` or `unix-abstract://`), and this code will return a ParsedTarget with an empty address. That can lead to emitting `server.address=""`, which is invalid/undesirable. Consider returning `null` when the parsed endpoint is empty (similar to `parseHostPort`), and add a unit test covering the empty-endpoint unix cases (including the single-colon form handled in `parseSingleColonScheme`).

Analysis: This module already has separate latest-dependency coverage. The library/testLibrary convention replaces gRPC 1.6.0 with the pinned latest release (currently 1.81.0) when `-PtestLatestDeps=true`. Existing `GrpcTest.successBlockingStub` calls `addClientInterceptor()` and asserts the captured client `server.address` and `server.port`, so that mode exercises `interceptWithTarget` and its proxy factory.

Upsides: Retains coverage against both the minimum supported gRPC version and the real current gRPC API without a duplicate stub or test configuration.

Downsides: The newer-path coverage remains part of the repository-wide latest-dependency job rather than the default minimum-version test run.

Addressed in 598a967bfffa2695a580f1da5b81ec4a8c95f541.

Analysis: GrpcRequest is part of the published gRPC library API. The pull request deprecates getLogicalHost() and getLogicalPort(), so CONTRIBUTING.md requires an Unreleased changelog entry. The new entry names both replacements and links to this pull request.

Upsides: Users scanning the next release notes can find the deprecated methods and migrate to getServerAddress() and getServerPort().

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [General] gRPC scheme lookup is case-insensitive, but these comparisons only recognize lowercase schemes. A valid target such as `DNS:///host:443` is accepted by gRPC (its resolver registry lowercases the scheme) yet is treated here as unknown, so `server.address` becomes the entire target and `server.port` is omitted. Normalize schemes for every comparison (while preserving the original target when it must be emitted) and cover uppercase DNS/Unix targets.

replies.body:
Addressed in 4707d7ae3da80c7721ebb5a0080c9f3e11dc3016.

Analysis: The parser used the target's original scheme for every known-scheme comparison, while gRPC treats resolver schemes without regard to case. The parser now normalizes only the extracted scheme with Locale.ROOT. It still passes the original target to DNS and Unix parsing and stores the original target for schemes such as IPv4 and xDS. Tests cover uppercase DNS and Unix forms through both URI and single-colon paths, plus uppercase preserved schemes.

Upsides: Targets accepted by gRPC now produce the same server address and port regardless of scheme case. Schemes emitted as the server address keep the spelling supplied by the caller.

Downsides: Parsing may allocate a lowercase scheme string. This runs once when the target-aware client interceptor is created, not for each RPC.

threads.body: [General] `URI.getAuthority()` includes userinfo, while Armeria strips userinfo before resolving the endpoint. For a supported URI such as `gproto+http://user:password@host:8080`, this passes the credentials into `GrpcTargetParser` and records them in `server.address` (and also loses the port because of the extra colon). Strip everything through the last `@` before creating the interceptor so telemetry matches Armeria's endpoint and cannot expose URI credentials.

threads.body: [General] A valid custom resolver target with a numeric opaque path, such as `consul:1234`, is classified as bare `host:port` here. gRPC accepts single-colon custom-scheme targets, so this emits `server.address="consul"` and `server.port=1234`; for an unrecognized scheme the RPC convention calls for preserving the whole target and omitting the port. Please distinguish authority-like inputs from actual target URIs (for example at the caller/API boundary) so numeric custom endpoints are preserved just like the existing `consul:orders` case.

threads.body: [Javaagent] This treats any letter-prefixed `host:port` as an opaque resolver target, but the javaagent passes the builder's raw target here. For `ManagedChannelBuilder.forTarget("localhost:50051")`, gRPC finds no `localhost` resolver and resolves it as `dns:///localhost:50051`; this branch instead emits `server.address="localhost:50051"`, omits `server.port`, and prevents the authority fallback. Armeria also passes URI authorities into this parser, so hostname authorities have the same failure. Please distinguish authority inputs at those call sites and mirror gRPC's resolver selection for raw builder targets (or capture the computed target).

threads.body: [Javaagent] For an IPv6 URI such as `http://[::1]:8080`, this constructs `dns:///[::1]:8080`. `java.net.URI` rejects raw brackets in a path, so `GrpcTargetParser` preserves that whole string and omits the port instead of emitting address `::1` and port `8080`. Use the raw authority (to retain escapes such as zone IDs) and percent-encode the IPv6 brackets before passing it as a DNS target.

threads.body: [General] Resolver selection is taken from the global registry, but gRPC's target-aware interceptor receives a target computed with the individual builder's resolver. With a per-builder custom resolver and target `consul:1234`, there is no global `consul` provider here, so this falls through to host/port parsing and emits `server.address="consul"` plus port `1234` instead of preserving the custom target and omitting the port. Distinguish computed targets from raw targets, or carry the builder's resolver selection into parsing.
